speaker: The Chairman
text: Head X, Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: As we know, at the heart of the Forward SG exercise, is an effort to engage as many Singaporeans as we can, from all walks of life, on how we should refresh our social compact on the road ahead for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It suggests, although unsurprisingly, that the aspirations of Singaporeans as to our social compact and to our way of life, has become increasingly diverse.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I say unsurprising because diversity has actually always been the bedrock of how our social compact came to be.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Our core values of building a caring and inclusive, multiracial, multicultural and multi-religious society remain sacrosanct among Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Closely related is our desire to celebrate our diverse cultural heritage in shared community spaces, expanding opportunities for all to excel or participate in arts and sports and to allow everyone the equal opportunity to pursue their dreams and aspirations.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: While it is undeniable that, as each successive new generation of Singaporeans come to the fore, we will continue to evolve as a society and refresh our social compact.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: These are some core values which should remain key tenets in the pillars of our social compact.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We must acknowledge, however, that Singapore, as a society, is rapidly evolving.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Increasing inter-ethnic and transnational marriages, may in the future, require us to rethink our racial and cultural classifications.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: An ageing population and a low birth rate may make us consider how we fundamentally function as a foundational unit that is entrusted with bringing up the next generation and caring for our seniors.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: This will decidedly have an impact on how we chart our way forward.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It is therefore apparent to me that how we manage the arts, heritage, culture, sports and community sectors within our society will have a deep impact on how our social compact will evolve moving forward.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat, please take both your cuts together.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In Malay, please. :   M3 celebrated its fifth birthday last year.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: When it began in 2018, the aim was to solve the Malay/Muslim community's problems by combining the expertise of MENDAKI, Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (MUIS) and the People's Association Malay Activity Executive Committees Council (MESRA) in the areas of education, religious life and community outreach respectively.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The good work done through M3 is evident.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Volunteer ambassadors under Project DIAN play an involved role in guiding vulnerable families, including early childhood development through methods and programmes developed together with the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) and KidSTART.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In late September, we at M3@Toa Payoh welcomed clinical psychologist Haikal Jamil, who generously held a concurrent physical and Zoom workshop for managing stress and burnout among residents. : Mr Chairman, in English, please.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My question to Minister is this: what does he see as some of the key outcomes of M3 and the role that active citizenry has played in this?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How does M3 amplify the efforts, compared to if MENDAKI, MUIS and MESRA undertook their respective initiatives alone?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I ask this especially as opportunities for cross-pollination of ideas already exist.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For example, the Community Leaders' Forum launched in 2003 is a platform to ensure efficient and effective management of resources by the various Malay/Muslim Organisations (MMOs) to avoid duplication of programmes and services.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: M3's wide range of different focus areas, together with the momentum of its programmes and initiatives in the past five years, gives it unlimited potential to attract individuals with different skills and interests.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And it is these diverse strengths we must harness to bring the Malay/Muslim community and Singapore forward, as our former President, Mdm Halimah, had stated at the Community of Success Conference last year.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What are some opportunities and key areas of need within M3, where volunteers can step forward and make a difference?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can we improve our capabilities in terms of sustainable volunteer management, and in terms of budgeting and human resources?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, in addition to the financial advisors, lawyers and healthcare professionals who help the community in their own area, we should broaden efforts to gather more professional groups from various industries – perhaps from emerging industries – who can lend their assistance or mentorship.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Second, we should scour for more Singaporean Malay/Muslims overseas who have done very well and flown Singapore's flag high.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They have unique perspectives in this age of internationalisation.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Third, we will need more online thought leaders, to participate responsibly in the increasing debates that are taking place on the Internet.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Wan Rizal, please take both your cuts.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This framework not only serves as a road map for the community, but it also reflects our nation's broader aspirations, as exhorted in the Forward SG exercise.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Through Forward SG, we have seen how Singaporeans' aspirations are now focused on the pursuit of meaning and purpose, and looking beyond themselves and helping others.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This collective aspiration represents what we wish for in our society, that is, a society where success is measured not only through an individual's achievements, but also through our contributions to the greater good.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Preventive health is a proactive measure that aims to improve the quality of life and reduce the burden of illness.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: More people are aware that lifestyle and daily choices can influence our long-term health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Furthermore, more people are interested in enhancing their understanding and activities in terms of mental health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Many recognise that mental health is just as important as physical health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This is a good time to look back on the measures that were taken and the journey forward to empower individuals to take ownership of their health, with support from the community.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In fact, it is a shared commitment that we must make as one people.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Therefore, we need to underscore the importance of creating a conducive environment that encourage, educate and enable every member of our community to lead a healthier life.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In this context, may I ask the Minister, what are the key initiatives of FA5, and how does it help to drive and advance our collective effort to improve our community's health – both physically and mentally?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The MBF then became the MBMF in 1984, after the establishment of MENDAKI Foundation, and the use of this fund was further expanded to include efforts and initiatives for community development.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In 2009, this fund was also extended for the use of upgrading and revitalising mosques.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: If this report will be produced, when will it be done?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: A complete and detailed progress report will enable, firstly, the community to have a deeper knowledge and understanding about the development and effectiveness of the programmes and initiatives that have been carried out, and secondly, so that the community can also know about the progress of M3's efforts in achieving the mission and vision that has been outlined for the Singapore Muslim community.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Syed Harun, please take your two cuts together.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In Malay, please. :   First, regarding MUIS' role in Muslim affairs, there are various complexities and diversity in today's world, especially with the rapid developments in the use of technology, such as the increasingly widespread use of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning and so on.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: From a religious perspective, the community faces a variety of complex issues, such as the latest technologies in medicine and food, as well as in the international financial systems and structure, as presented at the Fatwa Conference organised by MUIS recently.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We can see how international issues, such as the events in Israel and Palestine, Russia and Ukraine, as well as in the Middle East, can give rise to strong and considerable tension and emotions in society.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: There is also an additional dimension in Singapore, where the Muslim community is a minority group within a plural society.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: However, there is a desire among Muslims to further enhance their contributions, not only to issues that are near and dear to the Malay/Muslim community, but also to contribute to the nation and the wider Singapore society.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: There is also a desire, as well as expertise and knowledge from asatizah and members of the Muslim community to contribute their expertise and capabilities towards the religious affairs and benefit of the global Muslim community, for both the minority and majority groups.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Many turn to MUIS' leadership to provide clarifications and guidance to address challenges that Muslims face.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Is MUIS' current structure adequate and can it fully support the needs of the community in the future?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: What are the next steps to further enhance MUIS' competencies and capabilities, in order to produce a robust institution when facing contemporary challenges in Singapore?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Can we also increase support for local madrasah education as it is a pipeline for local religious scholars, in order to produce community leaders who can provide solutions to contemporary issues in Singapore in an appropriate, wise, credible and balanced manner?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Second, Chairman, I would like to ask about the success rate of M3's initiatives to date.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The implementation of M3 programmes has been encouraging, because it combines the resources across the three major community institutions, namely MUIS, MENDAKI and MESRA, in a way that multiplies their respective efforts, and this has benefitted the community.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I hope that Minister will be able to share, in particular, the result of all the good work and programmes under M3, and whether there are any early outcome measures to indicate that home ownership, health indices and accessibility to education, especially early childhood and post-secondary education – are improving within the Malay/Muslim community, and also whether there are any early outcome measures that indicate that drug abuse and crime recidivism rates are decreasing further among the communities and families engaged by M3.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: My view is that M3 should also focus on such outcome measures, and it should give attention to these indicators.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Certainly, it should be considered as one of the benchmarks of M3's success to ensure that the community’s progress and improvement are assessed objectively.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Nadia Samdin, would you like to take your two cuts together?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Religious and Malay/Muslim organisation leaders have been the guiding light for our community in navigating crucial challenges, whether in dealing with the global pandemic, technological developments and geopolitical issues, such as the ongoing crisis in Gaza.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They also play a role in representing our community, both nationally and globally.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A minority Muslim community in a country like Singapore faces unique challenges.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Asatizah and leaders of Malay/Muslim organisations play an important role in guiding the response of our community.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our actions and responses should recognise the context of Singapore's plural and multicultural society, based on religious principles.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What kind of support and resources are available to our religious and MMO leaders, in terms of training opportunities and global exposure, to broaden their experience and deepen their capabilities, to guide and unite our community? :   Serving the community is a never-ending task.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Leadership renewal plans are key in sustaining the impact that Malay/Muslim organisations have made over the years.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our community leadership remains crucial, especially at a time when the challenges that our society face are increasing and becoming more complex, such as climate change, online harms, mental well-being and so on.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that more from our generation will step forward to lead us to face these challenges.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Chairman, in Malay, please. :   In the ever-evolving landscape of community support and empowerment, initiatives such as the Bersamamu programme, stand as pillars of strength in nurturing resilient and harmonious Muslim marriages.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: This ground-up effort, spearheaded by Naib Kadis, extends its support to couples from the pre-solemnisation phase through their initial two years of marriage.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: By offering personalised guidance and assistance, Bersamamu not only lays the groundwork for a strong marital bond, but also addresses the evolving needs of Muslim families.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: With the recent enhancements to the programme, including the involvement of female asatizah, there arises a pertinent question - how does the Registry of Muslim Marriages (ROMM) and MUIS plan to further elevate the competencies of our Kadis, Naib Kadis and female asatizah, to better serve the multi-faceted needs of Muslim families in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In my speech during the AMLA amendment Bill, I shared about the importance in having the WMS as a sustainable revenue stream and how its returns can be used to prepare for medium- and longer-term needs of our community.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This includes ensuring that our madrasahs are supported with sound and sustainable funding, so that we can continue to offer quality education, provide different development pathways to enhance the skills of our religious teachers, as well as meeting the long-term needs of our mosques and madrasahs including land lease renewal.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Can the Minister share more about the plan to build the WMS corpus to ensure that we are prepared for the future needs of our community?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How can we encourage more of our community members to contribute to the WMS?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, in Malay, please. :   I have spoken previously about an ecosystem to develop wakaf in Singapore through a comprehensive dispute resolution framework.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am glad that this suggestion is being considered alongside more innovative plans for wakaf in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Mosque Wakaf Investment Plan (MoWIP), which was launched in 2022 with mosques in the West District, is an example of an innovative investment to generate good returns.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The AMLA was recently amended to enable MUIS to create the WMS.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The WMS will provide a sustainable source of revenue to support the socio-religious needs of our community in the long run.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The World Bank estimates that the value of wakaf assets globally has reached $100 billion.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Therefore, we should consider how to make the institution of wakaf in Singapore more attractive.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Currently, the income generated from wakafs vested in MUIS are exempted from the Income Tax Act.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, can MUIS, together with the Ministry of Finance and the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore, consider appropriate tax regimes that will incentivise Singaporeans to establish wakafs and attract foreign wakafs to relocate to Singapore?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In respect of the WMS, I would like to ask the Minister whether he can share the plans to build up the WMS corpus to prepare for our future needs?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Minister had also shared in his speech at last year' Hari Raya Get-Together that some in the community have pledged contributions to WMS.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can Minister provide an update on the status of pledges received so far?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And what are the plans to encourage our community to pledge and continue to contribute to the WMS? : The global halal market is projected to cross US$2.8 trillion by 2025 and Singapore is currently ranked seventh on the global Islamic economic indicator.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There is thus a huge growth potential opportunity in this sector.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These MOUs are significant for Singapore as it not only paves the way for Singaporeans to benefit from a wider range of halal-certified products entering our market but would also allow Singapore companies to bring their local halal-certified products overseas.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can the Minister elaborate on the significance of these halal internationalisation efforts for our minority Muslim community's success?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And what are the plans that MUIS may have with Ministry of Trade and Industry or Enterprise Singapore to get more businesses from Singapore to take full advantage of such agreements?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Besides this, there is also a potential to deepen expertise and skills among our community.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can the Minister share any plans to encourage more of our asatizahs and madrasah students to pursue such expertise in the halal industry?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Chairman, in Malay, please. :   A strong educational foundation remains a key pillar in helping both individuals and families achieve success and social mobility.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Could the Minister share how programmes, like KMM and MTS, have helped our students and how the programmes have grown over the years?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Beyond programmes like KMM and MTS, how can programmes like Learning Journey by MENDAKI's Future Series Team and M3@Pasir Ris-Punggol provide avenues for youths to explore the jobs in the growth industries?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How can we encourage more youths to attend such programmes, so that they can be inspired and learn more about opportunities in the growth industry? :   In his Budget speech, Deputy Prime Minister Wong shared that there will be many economic uncertainties ahead.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Therefore, to ensure that our Malay/Muslim workers continue to have good jobs, we must equip our workers with the knowledge and skills to be resilient, participate in growth industries and seize opportunities in the future economy.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Could Minister share whether there are plans to better support our Malay/Muslim workers to ensure that they are better prepared to thrive in the future economy?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Within our community, we have started professional networks, such as MMiT and MMs in Engineering.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The volunteers from MMiTs and MMs in Engineering have supported the programmes, such as Learning Journey, Raikan Ilmu and Hashtech.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In the Hashtech competition recently organised by M3@Pasir Ris-Punggol, volunteers from MMiT and MM in engineering assisted students to explore skills in AI.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Could the Minister also share how professional networks in our community can come together to share insights on the industry for students and potential mid-career switchers? :   Beyond educational support, mentoring plays an important role to equip our youth with emotional support and career guidance, so that they can achieve their aspirations.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Aside from mentoring programmes in educational institutions, M3 has also started to roll out mentoring programmes in some M3@Towns.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Could the Minister also share how these mentoring programmes could continue to be relevant and effective in supporting the needs and aspirations of our youths?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman, please take your three cuts together.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Chairman, in Malay, please. :   Sir, the recent study conducted by Yayasan MENDAKI sheds light on critical insights regarding employment and employability within the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: These findings present an opportune moment to recalibrate our approach towards lifelong learning initiatives and career development support within the community.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: How does the Ministry intend to leverage these insights to facilitate targeted interventions and support mechanisms, to ensure that individuals have the requisite skills and opportunities to thrive in an increasingly dynamic economy? :   Sir, it is crucial to acknowledge the invaluable role of volunteers in driving community-centric programmes and initiatives.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Volunteers, who often come from diverse backgrounds and walks of life, play a pivotal role in shaping the trajectory of community development efforts.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: However, encouraging greater participation in volunteerism, especially among beneficiaries of community support programmes, remains a pertinent challenge.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: What are the Minister's plans to inspire and incentivise individuals, including past beneficiaries of community initiatives, to step forward and actively contribute to the betterment of the community? :   Sir, the M3 framework, which is a collaborative effort between key community institutions, such as MUIS, MENDAKI and MESRA, has played a pivotal role in fostering unity and collective action within the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Through its citizen-centric approach and emphasis on impactful community programmes, M3 has served as a catalyst for meaningful contributions from professionals, community leaders and volunteers alike.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: As we reflect on the journey of M3 over the years, it becomes imperative to examine the key ways in which the framework has facilitated greater impact on the ground.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Could the Minister provide insights into some notable initiatives and collaborative ventures undertaken through the M3 framework, particularly highlighting successful partnerships with community stakeholders and volunteers?

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairman, our Malay/Muslim community has made significant strides since Independence and over the decades.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is a result of the collective and steadfast effort of everyone in the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As our Forward SG conversations have highlighted, this sense of care and contribution by everyone, regardless of race, language or religion, is key to strengthening Singapore's social compact.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Singapore Malay/Muslim Community's vision of a Community of Success is underpinned by "3C"s: Character, Competency and Citizenry.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is supported by M3, which marshals the strengths and resources of three institutions – MUIS, MENDAKI and PA MESRA – and our community assets to better serve the needs and aspirations of our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It has been about five years since M3 was set up.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Dr Syed Harun and Mr Faisal Manap asked about the progress and outcomes of M3.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through a more culturally nuanced approach that complements national efforts, we have been able to provide impactful programmes in the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The improvements have been made possible through complementary efforts by the Government and M3 community programmes like FITRAH to preventing re-offending.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: While it has been five years of M3, it would be too early to celebrate its success even as there are early and good indicators of it.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are continuing to review the impact of our programmes and will provide updates in due course.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: What is clear is that M3 has importantly provided the structure to nurture a culture of contribution within the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Volunteering, including through M3, is part of our national culture that is being celebrated by the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) this year.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To Mr Fahmi Aliman's and Dr Wan Rizal's queries, we have mobilised volunteers across the 11 M3@Towns to deliver greater impact on the ground and support last mile delivery.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: With a dedicated pool of over 850 volunteers at the M3@Towns, M3 has been able to tackle some of the key issues faced by our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: How can we take our Community of Success to greater heights?

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I believe this lies in a continued spirit of Citizenry, where we support one another to create a brighter future for our community and for Singapore, which my colleagues and I will speak more about today.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I will first share three strategies to fortify our Community of Success: first, encouraging a culture of giving back to build strong community institutions; second, empowering confident religious and community leaders to face contemporary challenges; and third, exemplifying citizenry on the world stage.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairman, in Malay, please. :   First, we must continue to ensure strong foundations for our religious institutions.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In turn, our religious institutions provide the moral foundation for our community to thrive in the economy.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Dr Syed Harun asked how MUIS can continue to support our community's future needs.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS established the WMS to generate a sustainable funding stream to support the future religious needs of the community, for the current and future generation.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These include our mosques, developing our asatizah and other community programmes.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Sharael Taha and Mr Zhulkarnain asked about the plans to build the corpus or principal fund for WMS.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS will expand this initiative to all mosques in other districts, so that they can grow their funds and amplify their impact on the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: While the spirit of gotong-royong has been part of our community's DNA, we need to be more organised and focused in multiplying efforts to encourage our community to contribute for the long term.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will work with the relevant agencies to study these proposals.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To Mr Sharael Taha's and Mr Zhulkarnain's queries, MUIS has embarked on a series of public education initiatives to equip the community with financial planning knowledge and tools to plan for their personal and family needs.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They can thus plan and contribute their excess income and wealth to WMS for the greater good, and reap perpetual rewards in the afterlife.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Since last year, MUIS has received WMS pledges amounting over $3.6 million from individuals, besides the investment of mosques.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am heartened by the community's response so far and I encourage more to contribute or pledge to WMS.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The MBMF provides for the development of all mosques including building upgrading and maintenance, where the allocation of funds are subject to each mosque's specific needs.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For all new mosques, all land and building cost are funded by the MBMF.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The MBMF also supports up to 75% of the approved cost for mosque upgrading.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I hope that contributions to WMS will help to foster a stronger culture of giving back within our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Senior Minister of State Zaqy will elaborate on how we can empower our community through MENDAKI's initiatives, and with the success that we achieved, we can contribute more actively.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu will share ways we can leverage opportunities for contribution through M3 as a community that has become an educated and talented community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, it is critical for our religious and community leaders to continue to have the knowledge, skills and experience, so that they are competent in guiding our community navigate the challenges ahead.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This includes developing our madrasah students who will be our future community leaders, as Dr Syed Harun mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As a matter of fact, in recent years, our asatizah have guided the community through difficult issues, such as the wearing of the tudung and the repeal of section 377A of the Penal Code.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ms Nadia Samdin asked about our plans to empower our asatizah to guide the community through contemporary issues.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As a minority Muslim community, we face a different set of challenges compared to Muslim majority countries.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In this regard, I agree with Dr Syed Harun that MUIS and our asatizah must provide clear leadership and guidance for our minority Muslim community living in such a contemporary context.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS has taken concerted efforts to grow bodies of knowledge and one recent initiative is the Fatwa in Contemporary Societies Conference held last month.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Eminent religious scholars from here and around the world discussed the importance of the fatwa institution and asatizah in providing robust solutions in the face of complex contemporary challenges.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Although Singapore is a small state with a minority Muslim community, internationally renowned Islamic institutions like Egypt's Darul Ifta' recognised our country's contributions in building bodies of religious knowledge.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This help to facilitate minority Muslims around the world to thrive in their respective contexts.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In fact, it also nurtures active citizenry in the respective societies.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is in line with the words of wisdom by the Grand Mufti of Egypt at the Fatwa Conference that minority Muslim communities should exemplify the spirit of active citizenry.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To further drive the development of our religious leaders and contextualised bodies of knowledge, MUIS will convene the second edition of the International Conference on Communities of Success (ICCOS) this October.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This Conference will focus on how citizenry and community leadership are underpinned by religious values, and add to the body of knowledge of how minority Muslim communities can thrive in plural societies.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At the same time, we must also raise the capabilities of our community leaders to offer effective support to families and the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Fahmi Aliman asked about our efforts to strengthen the competencies of our Kadi, Naib Kadi and female asatizah on the Bersamamu programme.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: More than 90% of them have undergone training to better guide couples in conversations on financial preparedness for marriage.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This helped them be more confident and empathetic in guiding couples.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will further develop their competencies in other areas, so that they can provide more effective support to couples.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will be commemorating the fifth anniversary of Bersamamu later this year.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The success of Bersamamu would not have been possible without the tireless efforts of our volunteer Kadi, Naib Kadi and female asatizah. : Mr Chairman, as a Community of Success, we take pride not only in actively contributing to society.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We also can demonstrate active citizenry on the world stage and bring distinction to our minority Muslim community and to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Such MOUs not only allow for halal-certified products from other countries to enter Singapore, but for Singapore companies to bring their halal-certified products overseas.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To Mr Zhulkarnain's query, MUIS works with our economic agencies to do so.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS will also explore opportunities for our asatizah to be involved in halal-related industries.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain also asked about the significance of this MOU for our minority Muslim community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This reflects the strong trust and confidence in our halal standards.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: More than just expanding business prospects, the MOU has enabled Singapore's minority Muslim community to stand tall in the world.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I was glad to join some Singapore business leaders to explore opportunities in Saudi Arabia in January.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: One of them was Mr Jimmy Soh, Managing Director of Growers Agri which exports rice and noodles, who shared with me that the MOU was a valuable commitment in promoting Singapore brands to the world.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Beyond efforts to strengthen halal cooperation, our minority Muslim community also contributes at the global stage, with how our religious leaders and institutions are internationally recognised for their thought leadership.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Congress plans to showcase Singapore's exemplary model for Muslim minorities to a global audience.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We hope that our model of thriving Muslim minorities in a modern, plural society will inspire other communities and pave the way for fostering peace and harmony globally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, our Malay/Muslim community has made significant progress in the last decade, especially in education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As the community's talent pool strengthens, it provides strong foundations for our community to contribute back and support one another as a Community of Success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI has played a key role in improving the education and professional development outcomes in our community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We do so in three ways: first, to strengthen education as a pillar for progress; two, empowering our community to thrive and contribute; and three, grooming the community leadership for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One of MENDAKI's key pillars is to provide support for our children and youths at all stages of their education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To achieve this, one of our main approaches is to mobilise talents and energise the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked about the progress of MENDAKI's signature programmes, like KMM and the MTS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Parental involvement has been an important part of KMM, to ensure that parents are empowered and confident to support their children's learning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: KMM's scale-up was possible with the help of targeted outreach and referrals by partners, such as Family Service Centres (FSCs), social service agencies (SSAs) as well as M3@Towns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: More KMM facilitators have also come on board, with their number tripling from about 50 in 2022 to more than 140 in 2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One KMM facilitator is Mr Irfan bin Ibrahim, a Year 3 student at the National University of Singapore (NUS), who started volunteering when he was serving his National Service in 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Volunteering shaped his decision to take up a degree in psychology and pursue a career in the social services sector to continue contributing to the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, MTS students are supported by 100 physical and virtual centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI has also continually sought to improve MTS offerings – such as by expanding its subjects offered to include Biology and Additional Mathematics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Fahmi Aliman has also asked how we could encourage and inspire more people to step forward and serve, especially those who have benefited and done well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI has many platforms for the community to contribute their skills and passion to meet the community needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: An example is how our steadfast MTS tutors have played an integral role in how MTS has grown from strength to strength.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One such tutor is Ms Anggreini Hamid, who benefited from MTS during her secondary school days.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Now a schoolteacher herself, she has been contributing back as an MTS tutor for the past 18 years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: She adopts innovative techniques to make her classes more engaging and effective for her students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Just a tidbit, all three of us – Minister Masagos, myself and Mdm Rahayu – have all been MTS tutors at some point of our lives too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, we have done our volunteer duty at some point to contribute back to our community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: At the post-secondary and tertiary level, MENDAKI's initiatives, such as the Youth Mentoring Office, help students realise their potential.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu will share more on these efforts in her speech.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Beyond a strong educational foundation, our Community of Success also needs a workforce that can secure good jobs and meaningful careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We want to empower our workers to thrive so that they can grow our community and our nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Fahmi Aliman and Mr Sharael Taha asked about our plans to better support Malay/Muslim professionals and workers in the future economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI continues to help our workforce develop their careers and professional networks, complementing national efforts by our tripartite partners in Government, employers and the Labour Movement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI initiated the Professional Networks to support Malay/Muslim professionals in growing their networks; to contribute back to the community; to exchange ideas; and to help younger workers enter growth industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We now have more than 450 Malay/Muslim professionals in these networks as at 2023 and MENDAKI will continue to encourage more professionals to join and serve as mentors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To Mr Sharael Taha's question, within both the Professional Networks and beyond, we now have about 1,000 Malay/Muslim professionals contributing across MENDAKI's initiatives – whether it is serving as KMM facilitators, MTS tutors, youth mentors or as speakers or human libraries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, in previous Committee of Supply debates, I shared about how corporate partners have partnered MENDAKI to provide scholarships for students to enter different industries from biomedical to finance, to aviation and technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We appreciate how companies also provide other forms of support, such as mentoring, to our students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: More than 50 MSD Pharmaceutical staff, such as data scientists, and those from the AI and Cybersecurity sectors, have signed up as mentors to 120 ITE students through the #amPowered@ITE programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, as our economy and workforce evolves, MENDAKI will continue to support our Malay/Muslim workforce in navigating career transitions and seizing future opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Through the M3 Focus Area 4 (FA4) on Employment and Employability, MENDAKI employs a community-based strategy by collaborating with M3 partners, including the NTUC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For women who wish to return to the workforce after a career break, MENDAKI's Women at Work (W@W) programme equips them with the relevant skills and connecting them with job opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One of them is Ms Siti Raudah, who was looking for a job to support her family and her three school-going children, after her husband was retrenched.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Siti joined the W@W programme in September last year, where she benefited from support, such as interview techniques and access to broader social and professional networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Earlier this year, Ms Siti found a job as an administrative executive in the oil and gas industry and shared that the programme has helped her to transit back into the workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, in Malay, please. :   Our third strategy is to grow and develop leaders not only for our community, but for our country as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Nadia Samdin asked for an update on the Tunas programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI started the Tunas Bersama M3 programme in 2022 to nurture the next generation of leaders of Malay/Muslim Organisations (MMOs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This 18-month programme not only equips emerging leaders with the knowledge, skills and networks to contribute and lead their own organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In fact, we want to support them in taking on larger leadership roles in our wider community in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One of the Tunas participants is NMP Dr Syed Harun, who ranks among our young MMO leaders today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, participants get to develop competencies in the areas of management, administration, fund raising, communications and change management, as well as the opportunity to be mentored by experienced senior leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The participants were able to apply the knowledge and skills that they gained to carry out seven community projects across the M3 Focus Areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, through Project Dream On, Tunas participants worked with professionals from MENDAKI's Professional Networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Their objective was to provide opportunities to Malay/Muslim youths, aged 15 to 17 years old, with sector-specific job shadowing opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This will help the youths to gain experience and expand their horizons in terms of future job opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The youth participants shared that this experience helped them gain confidence, exposed them to a variety of experiences and expand their range of interests, and help to better shape their future field of study and career plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Building on the positive outcomes of this programme, we will welcome our second batch of Tunas participants in April this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: That cohort will include leaders from MENDAKI's Professional Networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, MENDAKI will continue to support our Malay/Muslim community in reaching greater heights and empower the community to be active, contributing citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, each individual has a part to play to ensure that our community continue to progress together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I strongly encourage our Malay/Muslim workers to take up the opportunities to upskill through the initiatives that were recently announced during Budget 2024.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For instance, mid-career workers aged 40 and above who are looking at reskilling can consider the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This programme offers a SkillsFuture Credit top-up of $4,000 that can be used for selected courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Workers who wish to take on full-time diplomas at the polytechnics, ITE and arts institutions can also make use of the enhanced subsidies from the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: ITE graduates can also benefit through the ITE Progression Award of $5,000 upon enrolment to a diploma programme, and receive another $10,000 when they complete their studies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am confident that as a community, we can strengthen the culture of contributing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And in partnership with the Government and other community organisations, we can ensure our community achieve greater heights in education, professional development and leadership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: (In English): Our third strategy is to grow and develop leaders not only for our community, but for our country as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, over the last five years, we have worked hand-in-hand with our Malay/Muslim organisations to build up the M3 network.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The structures we have in place have enabled us to deal head on with various needs of our community, while complementing the Government's efforts at the national level.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A sense of Citizenry has been at the heart of what M3 has accomplished so far.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Entrenched within it is the culture of giving which will continue to be integral to our Community of Success.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have established a strong foundation for contribution through M3.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I will share three ways we can build on this legacy: first, equipping our youth for the future; second, empowering our community to take ownership of their health; and third, encouraging more volunteers to step forward and play a part.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mentoring is important as it guides our youths to realise their potential.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It can also be transformative when those who have benefited from the experience, pass it on, creating a virtuous cycle of giving.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To create a thriving mentoring culture in the Malay/Muslim community, we set up the Youth Mentoring Office, or YMO under MENDAKI, in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked how we ensure the continued relevance of our mentoring programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We conducted youth mentoring programmes in four M3@Towns at Jurong, Pasir Ris-Punggol, Tampines, and Woodlands last year, and will now be refreshing our approach to bring mentoring programmes closer to more youths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: One new mentoring programme we will be introducing at our M3@Towns, as well as mosques and Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) is "Cool Yah Conversations".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It adopts the concept of flash mentoring, a first of its kind approach in our mentoring programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Flash mentoring takes place over a shorter period and will combine interest-based activities like sports and games with impactful mentoring interactions in areas of personal development, educational transition, and career guidance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We hope that it will resonate with youths and lower barriers for them to get involved.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To Mr Sharael Taha's query, beyond mentoring programmes, MENDAKI also offers their Future Ready programmes which help youth better understand the changing work landscape and provide avenues for them to explore jobs in growth industries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Key to the success of these programmes are our passionate and dedicated youth mentors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Most have benefited from MENDAKI's many initiatives and now find ways to give back to the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In 2019, Arinna received MENDAKI's Special Achievement Award for Excellence and Anugerah Cemerlang MENDAKI.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, she works at the National Youth Council and has been a mentor to Nur Odelia Mohamed Azme since Odelia's second year of studies at ITE College Central through the #amPowered@ITE programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With Arinna's support, Odelia learnt to build self-confidence and take charge of her personal development.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Odelia is now working with MENDAKI's Care Advisors to explore potential post-tertiary pathways.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our youth mentors also join me and my fellow Malay/Muslim Members of Parliament including Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Ms Nadia Samdin and Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim in the YOUth@M3 Engagement sessions, and various M3@Town programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These include Youth Edge for vulnerable youth which Ms Mariam Jaafar advises, the Youth Network Mental Health Townhall that Dr Wan Rizal champions and learning journeys to STEM companies that Mr Sharael Taha organises.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I hope our youth mentors continue to inspire others to join our mentoring community in supporting others to realise their aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Chairman, in Malay, please. :   Health is a blessing and we have a responsibility to take ownership of it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Leading healthy lifestyles also enables us to be active citizens in our community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: One good role model who takes care of his health is Mr Iylia Shukor.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: He actively encourages our Malay/Muslim community to adopt a healthy lifestyle by organising health programmes for them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: When the fifth focus area of M3 was introduced last year, Mr Iylia tapped on the Saham Kesihatan programme to collaborate with more community partners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: He has since organised monthly five kilometres brisk walking events with Kembangan Chai-Chee Community Centre, Braddell Heights Constituency Office, Wisma Geylang Serai and Kassim Mosque, as well as Qigong sessions at community centres in M3@Geylang Serai.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Dr Wan Rizal asked how M3 initiatives spur efforts to take charge of our community’s health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Volunteers like Mr Iylia show how Saham Kesihatan can empower the Malay/Muslim community to drive their own health programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through Saham Kesihatan, they can receive support from M3 agencies, like PA MESRA and the Health Promotion Board, to implement programmes on health, including for mental well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Last year, over 500 participants took part in Saham Kesihatan programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To achieve this target, I invite more individuals, like Mr Iylia, to leverage on Saham Kesihatan, to bring health programmes to our Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Besides Saham Kesihatan, M3 agencies also work with HPB and the Jaga Kesihatan Jaga Ummah, or JKJU, network, where members regularly collaborate on initiatives that encourage healthier habits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We can expect more JKJU programmes at the M3@Towns throughout this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through JKJU and Saham Kesihatan, our Malay/Muslim community also contributes to the national Healthier SG campaign which aims to help all Singaporeans take ownership of their health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I hope we will embrace this responsibility towards our health as we strive for a meaningful future together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In looking to the future, we also take stock of how far we have come.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Dr Syed Harun asked whether M3 initiatives have led to improvements in community engagement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Since its formation five years ago, M3 has developed structures and built networks for us to help the community more effectively, including the vulnerable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With this framework in place, we need more volunteers to step up and help make M3 initiatives a success.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our volunteers comprise professionals from different fields who have been instrumental in the delivery of programmes at our M3@Towns – from initiating new programmes and befriending vulnerable families to connecting them with social assistance programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Therefore, we continue to ensure volunteers are equipped with the skills and knowledge to engage the community effectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through such workshops, they will learn to engage residents more meaningfully during house visits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The volunteers will also be able to increase their understanding of services at the national level, and therefore, help them to support residents in building strong and resilient families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, through Project DIAN, volunteers will provide holistic support for Malay/Muslim families residing in rental flats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They will also journey with these families to better understand their needs and connect them to the relevant services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: One such volunteer is Mdm Eryannie Mohamad, a Project DIAN Ambassador from M3@Geylang Serai who was motivated to encourage parents to take greater interest in early childhood development.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In November 2023, Mdm Eryannie and her fellow volunteers collaborated with MSR Interior Design to refurnish and repaint a beneficiary's home to provide a more conducive environment for their children's learning and family bonding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is also important for M3 to work closely with MMOs to deal with issues that may require a nuanced approach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, the Singapore Muslim Women's Association, or PPIS, provide support for Malay/Muslim women.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Indeed, MMOs play a key role at the community and national level, and we are happy to have more MMOs and partners come alongside us to support our families and community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We thank Mr Saktiandi Supaat for his suggestions on areas where volunteers can make a difference.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Allow me to share some of the volunteer opportunities within M3 that suit the interests and skillsets of those who wish to contribute.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our tertiary students can join the #amPowered programme as mentors for MTS students, or the "Cool Yah" programme at the M3@Towns.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: If you are a working professional, you can contribute your knowledge and experience as mentors or speakers for M3 youth mentoring programmes, or support other professionals through MENDAKI's Professional Networks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Those who want to contribute towards supporting children or vulnerable families can sign up as facilitators for our KMM initiative or as Project DIAN Ambassadors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I strongly urge my fellow Members to share these volunteer opportunities with your respective constituencies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: M3 will also be conducting volunteer recruitment drives throughout this year, and those who are interested can sign up via the M3 website or our socials. : A culture of contribution, driven by active citizenry underpins the spirit of M3.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Everyone of us has a stake in ensuring that we continue to thrive as a Community of Success.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There are many ways we can contribute in our different capacities, whether through pledging to the WMS, committing our time and effort as volunteers and mentors or even as a corporate partner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I hope that many more of us will step forward to join this noble cause to uplift our Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Chairman, in Malay. :   My colleagues and I have spoken on citizenry and our efforts to grow a culture of contributing back to society.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This will strengthen our community, so that we are more united and prepared to navigate the future.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: With geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainties, the path ahead of us will be challenging.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The issues we face will be more complex and can even be divisive, and it will also test our mettle and unity as a country.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Over the past few months, what has weighed heavily on our hearts is the situation in Gaza.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It has been heart-breaking for me, and many Singaporeans, to witness the humanitarian tragedy unfolding, and the suffering of many innocent civilians.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Bound by our shared humanity, we cannot help but carry with us their pain and suffering.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We may be miles away from Gaza, but we still feel connected in our hearts and minds, and we constantly pray for their well-being.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: From conversations on this crisis with the community, my Parliamentary colleagues and I hear the deep sense of grief, frustration and helplessness that many feel amidst the ongoing crisis.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We hope that Singaporeans will step forward and contribute generously.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The crisis may well be prolonged, and we do not know what will unfold in the coming days.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But we must continue to stand together and strengthen the unity that we share.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I am heartened that even during such a trying time, our community continues to embody the spirit of citizenry, as Singaporeans providing a whole-of-society support to the Palestinians in our uniquely Singaporean way – contributing to dialogue, giving generously to humanitarian aid, praying for the victims of war, and not forgetting how we can strengthen solidarity with one another.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As Muslims welcome the blessed month of Ramadan next week, let us also intensify our prayers for peace and protection – not only for the people in Gaza, but also elsewhere in the world and here at home. : Mr Chairman, in conclusion, I would like to thank Members for your support and suggestions on how we can continue to deepen our citizenry and grow a culture of contribution.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: By working together with our community partners, I am confident that we will strive towards a Community of Success and contribute to a bright future for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank Minister and Senior Minister of State and Senior Parliamentary Secretary for her answers to my cuts and for their speeches.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: He mentioned in his last speech about the efforts and I think he gave a very heartfelt speech about the issues that we face in Gaza and in Palestine.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: He mentioned about how Rahmatan Lil Alamin will be coming on stream, especially during Ramadan.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Can Minister share a bit more whether this second round, whether there will be a time limit?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Because the previous one, Rahmatan Lil Alamin there was a period of time where they can collect donations, whether this time round, can Minister share so that the community and public can know a bit more about that?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: And how does RLAF plan to reach out to the community, especially during Ramadan and may be beyond that as well?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Second question, Mr Chairman, I think Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu and Senior Minister of State Zaqy mentioned about working with corporates.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I think there is only so much that the Government can do as part of a social compact.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I was wondering whether there is more that corporates can be involved, whether Malay/Muslim corporates or maybe non-Malay/Muslim corporates, how they can actually help the Malay community going forward beyond scholarships that Senior Minister of State has mentioned and beyond the specific volunteerism sort of efforts that Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu has mentioned, whether there could be — well, our efforts to actually entice a bit more of the Singapore corporates to help our community going forward?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation, like any other organisations, when they want to raise funds – particularly for an overseas purpose – need to regularise, get its permits in place and it will take time.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But it will also be time limited by the permit and that was why in the previous exercise of collecting the funds, it was time-limited.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I think it is the right thing to do.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At the same time, we want to ensure that there is a time where we can focus our efforts in raising these funds.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But we must also be able to move on to do other important things for our community and for everyone else.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And we will raise this awareness about when it starts and when it will end during our Friday sermons as well as through the media.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Chairman, I will take the second question Member Saktiandi Supaat asked earlier.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
