speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They will also Learn-to-Play Programmes, such as Yes!

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I Can and Play-Ability Festivals, where both persons with disabilities as well as persons without those disabilities can come together and play sports together, and take part in sports, such as swimming, badminton, basketball, archery and shooting.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: SportSG is also developing an inclusive Train the Trainer programme, which will be a more structured programme to equip fitness instructors with the relevant skills to guide PwDs and recommend appropriate, suitable exercises for them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We therefore fully agree with Mr Ong Hwa Han that beyond just setting up the hardware, what matters is how empowered PwDs feel when they exercise in the public setting and come to our gyms and come to our pools at ActiveSG.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua will elaborate more about our initiatives to make sports even more accessible to all.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, let me turn next to high-performance sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Overall, Team SG athletes have done well in 2023.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There were also eight Games records, 17 national records and 40 personal bests achieved by Team Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But what is even more encouraging is that we continue to field a young team.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Athletes under the age of 24 made up the majority of the contingent and they delivered outstanding performances.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Also, critically, 30% of our gold medals were won by debutant athletes at the SEA Games.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the Asian Para Games 2023, our athletes delivered their best away performance of all time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: With eight medals, they shattered collectively, nine national records – including two Asian Paralympics records and achieved 12 personal bests.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We now have our sights set on the next major Games for the year, which will be the Olympics and Paralympics in Paris.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Many Members have spoken about how we support our elite athletes in high-performance sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, let me come back to this point.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are constantly on a mission to find our next sporting champion and to create as many options and pathways as possible for athletes to reach their peak.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Champions like Singapore kitefoiler Maximilian Maeder, who is one of the Team Singapore athletes who will be at the Olympics this year.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: He won a gold at the Formula Kite Youth World Championship in July 2023.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: He followed that on with a gold in the Asian Games, winning all 16 of his races on his way to that gold medal.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: He is the first Singaporean to be nominated World Sailings' Male Sailor of the Year.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: He is all of 16, going on 17 years old.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: He is leaving this evening for further training in Europe in preparation for the Olympics.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is so that they can be full-time athletes and free from distractions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: On top of this, we also provide funding for their training and their travel overseas for competitions, or indeed, even if the competition is in Singapore here.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They are further supported by a sports science team in areas, such as sport biomechanics, nutrition, sports psychology, physiotherapy and physiology as well.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We work with them on a curated coaching programme: help them with their diet, with sleep, with recovery, with preparation; just about everything that we need to get an athlete in peak performance.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will continue to strongly support their quest for sporting excellence, as Mr Darryl David and Dr Syed Harun mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But for every athlete who has found success, there will be many more, just below at the next tier, aspiring to find their next peak.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will endeavour to support them on their journey too.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I spoke earlier about broadening the base, and I think this is a critical starting point if we want a strong and sustained pipeline of talent coming through for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We, therefore, work with the national sports associations (NSAs), with schools, as well as with private sporting academies, to identify and track good talent, give them a structured framework for development, with good coaching and mentorship.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our second key strategy is then to put these talents through a structured development pathway, with a comprehensive support programme either by Sports Science Institute or by the NSA.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Take, for example, the Singapore Table Tennis Association (STTA).

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Their Junior Development Squad (JDS) is one good example.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Over the years, they built up a strong pipeline of local talents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We now have Koen Pang, we have Zhou Jingyi and we have Izaac Quek, all graduating from STTA's JDS.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: STTA and the Singapore Sports School also work closely together to set up the School Within a School programme.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This programme enables our student table tennis athletes to get extended training twice a day, with a customised academic support programme that is worked around their sporting needs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, if they need to make up classes, they need to do courses outside of competition period, this programme helps them to catch up, helps them to keep on par with their classmates.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We invest not just in the training of our athletes, but also support their sporting journey throughout their education and, eventually, their employment as well.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For athletes still in school, the spexEducation programme helps them manage, both sport and education, by supporting them with school admissions, scholarships and also trying to schedule classes around trainings and competitions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For athletes who have finished with school and are seeking to enter the workforce, they can apply to our spexBusiness partners, and they include corporates, like Grab, CapitaLand, DBS and Quest Ventures.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But of course, we can do more and we can encourage more corporates to come onto the programme, because this programme is really as strong as the number of corporates who enter the programme with us.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition, when athletes need to go for training, even if they are not on the spexBusiness programme, there is spexTAG, which stands for spex Training Allowance Grants, to help athletes defray training costs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And for those who miss work while training for or competing or taking part in overseas competitions and major games, spexGLOW offsets lost wages.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, this is the programme that we have to support an athlete on their path, even as they manage work and school together, with training for their sport.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I spoke earlier about how we had good young athletes at SEA Games, debutants who won a third of our gold medals.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will give them even more support to realise their potential.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Next, let me turn to Mr Xie Yao Quan and Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, who asked about our plans for Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I have spoken at some length earlier this week on the Sports Hub and will not repeat the points.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Kallang Alive is a bigger precinct, Sports Hub occupies about a third or so of that space.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, we have got a lot more potential at Kallang Alive.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Against that backdrop, Mr Xie says that we should continue to bring major sporting events to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Sports Hub is already well poised to host many of these events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition to the suite of facilities within the Kallang Alive precinct, such as OCBC Arena and the Aquatic Centre, there will be new facilities ready soon, like the Kallang Football Hub and the Kallang Tennis Centre.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The latter includes 12 outdoor, seven indoor and two mini tennis courts, that will complement the facilities at the Sports Hub, as we plan for more world-class sporting events at the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For our TeamSG athletes, hosting such events will also mean more opportunities for them to compete.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They get more wild cards when the event is held in Singapore and they test themselves, measure themselves up against some of the world's best, right here, on our home ground.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Singaporeans will also get to watch more of the world's best athletes in action, adding to an already vibrant sporting calendar.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It also boosts economic growth and global recognition, possibly unlocking latent potential in hosting entertainment and sporting events, and concurrently strengthening Singapore's reputation as a choice destination for high-signature international events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This segues nicely into Mr Sitoh's point about the Singapore Indoor Stadium, or the SIS.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The hosting of high-quality international events is valuable and also highly sought after.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our competitors are not standing still and we, likewise, must continually innovate and evolve if we want to continue to attract top-tier events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The SIS is part of the Sports Hub, but it was built in 1989 and is now more than 30 years old.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have gone around to study some of the best arenas in the world, to learn from them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are considering an arena that can host more sophisticated events, that can also flexibly accommodate different types of events and have a faster turnaround time between the different types of events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It will be different between sports and entertainment and you have to turn it around very quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This location will continue to give the new arena a synergistic connection to the rest of the Sports Hub and Kallang, and also allow us to plan events and programming as an entire precinct, benefiting from the economies of scale.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It will also allow the current SIS to operate until the new indoor arena is operational and this minimises disruption to the pipeline of events and programming, which can continue throughout the construction period for the new arena.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will study plans for the SIS and provide more details when it is ready.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are currently studying the capacity of this new indoor arena, taking into account existing and upcoming venues.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It should, in our view, have at least the same capacity as the current SIS and also be future-proofed, so that it can continue to serve Singapore's interests in the foreseeable future.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The new indoor arena will operate alongside the rest of the Sports Hub, offering synergies with the other sporting and community facilities at the Kallang Alive precinct, and also seek to inject further vibrancy into the precinct.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Usha Chandradas made an impassioned speech yesterday evening and asked about our plans to transform and grow the arts ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To quote one of our Cultural Medallion recipients, poet Prof Edwin Thumboo, he says "Art, whatever its form, helps to define the texture, the rhythm, imagery, symbolism, energy of life in society." And that is why the arts is so important in our society.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Singapore is a multicultural society, where the tapestry of our nation is so woven by the colourful threads of our unique diversity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And because of this, we have a special heritage to preserve, which in turn, spawns its own unique art forms in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is not everywhere in the world that you can enjoy poetry in a range of different languages, all of which we can associate with, including dialects and Singlish, and have both traditional and contemporary forms of dance, music, theatre and visual arts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Santha formed friendships with other dancers, who were also Cultural Medallion winners, like the ballet-trained Goh Lay Kuan, as well as the Malay dancer, Mdm Som Said.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They learnt each other's dance styles, appreciated the beauty of each other's culture, which they then infused into the expression of their own craft.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I think that is unique, that is special, that is Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This story reflects a distinctive feature of our arts and culture sector that we must continue to cherish, the shared multicultural diversity that Mr Sitoh Yih Pin spoke about.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, we will continue to support our arts practitioners.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It has become more vibrant and arts appreciation more widespread.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have also developed top-class national institutions, like the Esplanade, National Gallery of Singapore, Singapore Art Museum, STPI Creative Workshop and Gallery, complemented by a rich array of private institutions, like the ArtScience Museum and The Private Museum, as well as private spaces, Artspace@Helutrans.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And we have a number of established arts companies today, reflecting the diversity of culture that I mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Companies like Nadi Singapura, Bhaskar's Arts Academy, Ding Yi Music Company, which offer a range of different art forms, genres, representing all of us, a diverse cross section of Singapore's ethnic and cultural make-up.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the same time, our homegrown artists are rapidly establishing themselves on the world stage and bringing Singapore to the world.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Multidisciplinary artist Robert Zhao will be showcasing his work titled "Seeing Forest" at the upcoming Venice Biennale 2024.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Biennale is amongst the world's most prestigious platforms to showcase contemporary art.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our young singer-songwriter, Shazza, was featured at the iconic New York Times Square billboard just last year, as part of Spotify's EQUAL campaign, which spotlights women in music from around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Singapore Chinese Orchestra presented "Legends of Nanyang" in Shanghai, and later this year, they will be in Suzhou, Tianjin and Beijing.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Singapore Ballet will also open the Gala event at Washington's Kennedy Center's "10,000 Dreams: A Celebration of Asian Choreography".

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And this will happen in June 2024 and they will present the late Cultural Medallion recipient Goh Choo San's choreography, "Momentum".

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Singapore Symphony Orchestra has been invited to perform in Japan, and they will take part in the Kyoto Concert Hall in October 2024, an invitation by the Asia Orchestra Week.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These festivals have drawn a strong international crowd and at the same time, they also allow Singaporeans to access the best in the world, as they come into Singapore and exhibit in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Singapore Art Week, or SAW, for example, has grown annually to encompass more areas and districts in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Arts businesses, like art galleries and ceramic studios, have actively participated in SAW, to grow access to new audiences and new markets.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: If you are a young creative today, there are many more pathways to pursue an arts education and make something out of it.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The School of the Arts, or SOTA, our first specialised pre-tertiary arts school, was set up precisely to do this.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The School of the Arts (SOTA) graduates go on to pursue careers in the arts or tap on their arts-enriched educational experience to embark on diverse careers.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the tertiary level, those interested in the arts can also pursue diploma programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Take, for example, Republic Polytechnic's School of Technology for the Arts, or courses at the School of Art, Design and Media at the Nanyang Technological University, Yong Siew Toh Conservatory at the National University of Singapore for those inclined, or the degree programmes offered by Singapore's first arts university, the University of the Arts Singapore (UAS), that was established as an alliance between local arts institutions, LASALLE College of the Arts, as well as the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They will welcome their first intake in August this year.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Both these arts institutions have an impressive faculty and alumni who have earned national recognition and also championed Singaporean creativity on the global stage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MCCY and the National Arts Council (NAC) have been working closely with the Ministry of Education (MOE) and UAS to ensure that there will continue to be good opportunities for arts graduates because it is one thing to have these courses and programmes, but it is another to ensure that when they graduate and they finish with their education, that there is a space for them in the creative economy.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And it is the creative economy which I now turn.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These education pathways have built up a strong pipeline of talents which can flow into our creative economy where the range of job options have also expanded.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I want to give Members one example: Guo Ningru.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: She is a sound engineer with more than a decade of experience designing sound for both local and regional productions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I met her when she won the Young Artist Award a couple of years ago in 2022.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ningru pursued a degree at the LASALLE College of the Arts, specialising in Sound Design.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: She received NAC's National Arts Scholarship and furthered her education at the renowned Sound Design programme at the University of California Irvine.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As a creative entrepreneur, Ningru creates 360-degree soundscapes, where audiences are immersed in an aural world.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But what struck me about Ningru is a young creative, passionate about a very discrete area of the arts – sound engineering, how we deliver sound from the stage to the audiences.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: She developed a deep passion and interest in it and she is now highly schooled, well-educated in this area.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: She is now working in this area, freelancing, working with different companies, both local as well as regional, embarked on a career as a creative entrepreneur.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And that is what we want to see.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Working in a wide range of roles, arts SEPs primarily take on gig work and generally do not have structured support from employers to support their training or career development.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But they are very critical to the continued success and growth of the arts ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They can also look forward to a wider range of development opportunities curated to fit their training needs and the nature of their work.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Increasing support will help arts SEPs seize better work opportunities across a broader and wider range of job roles and, in turn, boost the long-term growth of the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Minister of State Low will speak a bit more about this.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But things changed quickly when COVID-19 intervened and we saw some shifts in the operating environment as well as trends, for example, audience preferences and new modalities of art presentation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There was also greater intersection of sectors like design, fashion, film, architecture and music.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They came together in ways which, perhaps, we did not see earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Some of these shifts have also become permanent ones.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But in all of them, we saw opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, rather than keep with the old plan and let it run its course, we took the opportunity to refresh the plan immediately, with Our SG Arts Plan last year, after substantial consultations with artists, stakeholders and so on in the sector for some time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Drawing an analogy from the arts, we changed the script during the intermission because we saw those shifts and we thought why not move down, move quickly, do not waste time and get the arts ecosystem powered and ready for the next bound.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is in addition to the existing funding to the arts and heritage sector already provided by the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Minister of State Low will speak a bit more about this in her speech the details.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But I want to close this section with an appeal.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have seen how our arts ecosystem has grown and evolved over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our practitioners and arts companies have also matured, evolving with our society, challenging us with arts which tells our story, manifesting our fears and reflecting our dreams.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have young creatives being given options to enter the creative workforce and, like Ningru, grabbed them with both hands and made a real fist of it.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also have many artists who are performing on the international stage, knocking on the door of world recognition.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have consciously nurtured arts patronage and support from donors who are playing their part to sustain the arts, supported by Government funding and programmes, such as the Cultural Matching Fund, which we extended a couple of years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is what would really help our artists level up and scale even greater heights, a collective appreciation in support by the Singaporean audience.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They need this collective support and, together, I believe we can harness its transformative power to then uplift our entire nation and build on the strengths of our diversity and multiculturalism to achieve social cohesion and a stronger sense of national identity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We do not live or achieve our dreams alone, but together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is true of our athletes and artists in the way which I have sketched out.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And for all of us, we are our heroes as well, telling stories which inspire us.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, in the spirit of Forward SG, we want a society where no one is left behind; where those who succeed give back and invest in the dreams of others, pay it forward; where everyone brings more to the table and, as a result, we all get more in return, where we are all collectively stronger than the sum of our parts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are stepping up our efforts to promote civic engagement and giving back.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will also consciously provide more space for citizens to lead the change they want see in the areas that they care about and the Government will come in to support them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: My colleague, Minister of State Alvin Tan, will share more on these efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, there is no one Singapore dream, no uniform pathway for success.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I also want to thank, in particular, my team from MCCY and our agencies who work very hard to ensure that the policies that we devise meet the needs of Singaporeans and come closer and closer to the endpoints that I mentioned earlier – for cohesion, identity and a transformative strength that is Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: That is why we will continue to work hard to build a vibrant and cohesive home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, the arts and heritage serve as powerful ways to connect Singaporeans of different backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government works closely with our arts and heritage practitioners, stakeholders and the public to create and foster a vibrant arts and heritage ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In my speech today, I will share how we aim to bring Singapore's arts and heritage to the next bound of growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First, we will open up more diverse touchpoints to widen Singaporeans' access to arts and heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Second, we will support the development of our practitioners and boost their artistic excellence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Third, we will build a more robust arts and heritage ecosystem to bring the sector to greater heights.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In recent years, we saw sustained and holistic efforts to expand access to the arts, develop a wider audience and enrich our heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC provided grants and arts housing subsidies to support the creation and production of artistic works, foster organisational growth and cultivate audience engagement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, earlier on, Minister Edwin Tong talked about the Singapore Art Week or SAW.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: SAW reached over 1.4 million attendees in 130 events last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And this year, SAW 2024 featured 183 events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Partners from different sectors, like Marina Bay Sands, HDB and Singapore Airlines, worked with us to bring Singapore art to wider audiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To promote and preserve our heritage, we opened the revamped Peranakan Museum last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And in addition, we joined Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand to jointly nominate the kebaya to be on the UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last year, we unveiled Our SG Arts and Heritage plans for 2023 to 2027, like what Minister Edwin Tong mentioned, envisioning an inclusive, accessible and vibrant arts and heritage sector for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We aim to create a connected society, foster a creative economy and establish Singapore as a distinctive city.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: At the same time, our SG Heritage Plan 2.0 seeks to empower the community to safeguard and promote our shared heritage and encourage active participation in shaping our heritage landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will build the growth of our heritage sector upon the foundational blocks of identity, industry, innovation and community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government is committed to the success of these plans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Usha Chandradas would be glad to know that this $100 million provided is on top of the annual budget for arts and heritage and will go towards: one, expanding arts access for Singaporeans; two, developing our artists and arts workers in Singapore; and three, building a robust arts ecosystem where arts companies and artists thrive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, we will look at making more significant investments in bringing the arts to the community, catalysing new spaces in our city and leveraging the arts for social impact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will further support arts groups to achieve excellence, for instance, by catalysing innovation, expanding into new audience segments and building common new capabilities through technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC will expand access to the arts for Singaporeans so that all can participate and benefit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We want to extend the reach and the significance of the arts sector to Singaporeans across diverse walks of life and socioeconomic backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides widening access, we will unpack the power of the arts to promote the health and wellness of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Yesterday evening, Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Mohd Fahmi have shared, super-ageing Singapore can certainly gain from arts programmes that seek to enhance the quality of life and personal wellness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We, in MCCY and NAC, agree with both Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Mohd Fahmi.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have had good feedback from such programmes and will continue to do more in this area.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It will initially focus on the well-being of our seniors, with plans to subsequently expand its scope to reach wider groups of people.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The framework and the resources will open up more opportunities for our arts practitioners to use their craft to support and promote well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This move is also aligned with our aim to increase access to the arts for citizens through health and community touchpoints, further supporting the Government’s HealthierSG objectives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The National Heritage Board (NHB) will continue partnering with social service agencies on heritage-based interventions targeted at improving well-being, especially that of our seniors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is part of the focus on community under Our SG Heritage Plan 2.0.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To give Members a quick example, I think some of you may have visited the National Museum.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The National Museum of Singapore recently created an inclusive social space that is called Reunion, for our seniors, including those with mild cognitive impairment and dementia, to engage in meaningful activities and conversations inspired by the museum’s collection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, besides engaging our seniors through the arts, we are also actively engaging our youth in the plans for promoting and safeguarding Singapore’s heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I agree with Mr Keith Chua and Mr Sitoh Yih Pin on the importance of strengthening our youths' understanding and appreciation of our shared legacy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This gives our youth a platform to share their views and a chance to shape our museums and heritage landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through these initiatives, we hope to make the arts and heritage accessible for all Singaporeans across different age groups, ensuring meaningful engagement with our cultural heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, as part of our aim to widen access to the arts, NAC will further expand the diversity of arts spaces in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is in line with our goal to make Singapore a distinctive city.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Darryl David would be glad to know that NAC will continue to collaborate with public and private sector partners to unlock arts spaces for our artists and also our arts organisations, while also enlivening our public spaces with the arts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, NAC works with the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) on the Community and Sports Facilities Scheme, which co-locates community, arts and sports spaces with commercial developments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Recently, The Artground, which is an inclusive family-oriented arts space for children opened at the One Holland Village mall.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This not only offers Singaporean families' easy access to quality arts experiences but also enhances the vibrancy of commercial spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To create more touchpoints for the arts, NAC will continue to collaborate with public sector and private sector partners to unlock and develop arts spaces across Singapore, including the use of both new and also refurbished spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC has been working with the arts community and stakeholders to co-create the vision for the redevelopment of this space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It is being developed as a hub for artistic experimentation and to support the work of young and emerging practitioners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We thank Ms Usha Chandradas for her feedback when she delivered her cut last evening.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: When completed in two years' time in year 2026, 45 Armenian Street will provide about 14,000 square feet space for the arts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, besides having greater access to the arts in a variety of spaces, Singaporeans are also gaining a deeper appreciation of our heritage assets at different spots across the island.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Mark Lee, Mr Darryl David and Mr Sitoh Yih Pin asked about our plans to foster community bonding, national pride and enliven neighbourhoods through our heritage assets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As part of Our SG Heritage Plan 2.0, NHB will launch Heritage Activation Nodes, or HANs, in various neighbourhoods island-wide.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Together with community partners and heritage interest groups, we will co-create heritage activities and celebrate the unique heritage of our neighbourhoods in each HAN.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I was hoping that Dr Tan Wu Meng will be in the House when I say that about the second HAN in Clementi.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Behind the development of the Katong-Joo Chiat HAN is Katong Culture, a heritage interest group from Joo Chiat Community Club Management Committee and their community partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through these nodes, we hope to encourage greater appreciation of our heritage assets among Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The HANs will offer fresh heritage touchpoints and provide the platform and opportunities for Singaporeans to co-create heritage experiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, I will now touch on how we will create a vibrant arts and heritage ecosystem with a strong core of arts and heritage businesses and practitioners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As I mentioned earlier, NAC will be investing an additional $100 million over the next four years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Under the Creative Economy Thrust of our SG Arts Plan 2023 to 2027, the funding will be used to grow our arts ecosystem and help our local arts companies scale impact and speed up their transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will further support our artists and arts companies to develop distinctive and diverse arts offerings for both local and international audiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC will support transformations in art making and artistic productions that leverage on technology to catalyse innovative arts products.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC will help our arts companies to expand their reach or cultivate new audience segments through engaging and innovative works or presentations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC will partner with individuals, including independent content creators and writers, as well as organisations, on joint projects and initiatives to expand the overall audience base.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will use technology as an instrument to achieve our goals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It is an important learning point from COVID-19 that we intend to continue to harness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, NAC’s Catch, which is a one-stop online destination for all things arts and culture in Singapore will help our artists and arts organisations to: one, promote their work; two, reach a wider audience; and three, to build relationships with potential supporters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, technology can empower us to better understand consumers’ preferences and tastes through data collection as well as analytics.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, with this knowledge, we will be then more equipped to grow the arts and culture scene strategically.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To create a vibrant arts and heritage ecosystem, we need a strong core of practitioners with talent, capabilities and skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many of our arts practitioners are self-employed persons, or SEPs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Minister Edwin Tong announced earlier, NAC will strengthen the support for our Arts SEPs to boost their prospects and their chances of success.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will enhance and increase their training opportunities to enable them to pursue their profession with better career stability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC will develop multiple pathways of training and support for Arts SEPs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This can be in the form of workplace-based, peer-to-peer and also self-directed learning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Arts Resource Hub will also be enriched with career guidance resources and content tailored for Arts SEPs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, NAC worked with Jeremiah Choy, an SEP and creative director, producer and curator to produce a series of videos with tips and best practices on how to set up a business in the arts and be a successful freelancer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, NAC will widen the funding access for Arts SEPs to receive training opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These training support enhancements will certainly benefit SEPs, including the arts instructors, as Ms Jean See had pointed out during the delivery of her cut last evening.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I would also like to assure Ms Jean See that NAC works with the National Instructors and Coaches Association (NICA) through the NAC-NICA Training Support programme, providing our SEPs with training subsidies and training allowances to support their upskilling journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC also provides affordable physical spaces for arts SEPs and arts instructors’ use via the Arts Resource Hub (ARH).

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To maintain a vibrant arts and heritage ecosystem, we will continue to honour and celebrate the peaks of artistic excellence in our midst.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Cultural Medallion (CM), as the nation’s highest arts accolade, provides funds to support its recipients’ continuous artistic pursuits and contributions to the Singapore art scene.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We would like to assure Ms Usha Chadradas that NAC has, over the years, broadened the range of projects that the CM Fund can support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I also want to assure her that the process for the recipients to utilise the Fund has also been simplified.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, please allow me to speak in Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In Mandarin):   Chairman, the arts and culture reflect our daily lives, connecting Singaporeans from different social backgrounds and fostering a sense of unity and identity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It is an important part of our social and national development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last year, MCCY launched Our SG Arts and Heritage Plans 2.0.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This funding will help us to expand the scope of arts, increase opportunities for Singaporeans to engage with arts, nurture more artists, and establish a more comprehensive arts ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MCCY has always been committed to bringing arts and culture to more Singaporeans so that more can participate in and benefit from the activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This year, we can look forward to even more vibrant and robust arts and heritage offerings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These two Heritage Activation Nodes will unlock more heritage touchpoints for Singaporeans, promoting greater understanding and appreciation of the unique heritage of their neighbourhoods, and allow all to jointly experience and create unforgettable memories together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC and healthcare partners will work together to integrate frameworks and resources to guide artists and community partners in the design of arts and cultural programmes that can help to uplift spirits, cultivate Singaporeans’ interest and passion in arts, enrich our lives and making them more meaningful.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This programme will be developed first through pilots with seniors and expanded thereafter for more communities to benefit from arts for well-being programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, MCCY is committed to working with our artists and partners from various fields to build a vibrant and dynamic arts and heritage sector for Singaporeans, as well as a harmonious, inclusive, creative, cohesive and uniquely charming Singapore. : Chairman, our arts and heritage belong to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Minister Edwin Tong mentioned, everyone can support and everyone contribute to the vibrancy of our arts and heritage ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, MCCY, NAC, NHB, we invite all our stakeholders to co-create a dynamic and flourishing Singapore arts and heritage scene together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Chairman, our Forward SG exercise brought together over 200,000 Singaporeans to share their hopes and dreams for Singapore and how they can contribute towards our refreshed social compact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our community and corporates have answered this call.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Today, I will share how MCCY is creating more spaces, more platforms and more tools for them to give back and shape a better Singapore – a city and nation that inspires, as Minister of State Low Yen Ling just said in her speech.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our community's response to the call to shape a better Singapore starts early on – with our youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As Deputy Chair of the National Youth Council (NYC), I get to spend a lot of time with our youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They are hungry; they are inquisitive; and they have diverse dreams and passions, ideas and ideals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Dr Syed Harun and I know this in our work with our youths at NYC, and I thank him for serving alongside me as an NYC council member.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Dr Harun and I know that our youths have an unwavering can-do attitude and spirit and want to take action.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They care deeply about giving back and making a positive impact on the causes they believe in.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: That is why we have been listening to them – listening to what they want and providing them with the space, support and the platforms to lead this change.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Hany Soh asked how we are supporting our youths to experiment and execute their ideas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: She specifically mentioned the Youth Action Challenge, or YAC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These projects have created positive outcomes in our community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Recently, I spent an evening with Grace, Jun Han and Valencia from Friendzone, a social enterprise that organises events to connect people and to build new friendships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Since receiving funding in YAC Season 2, Friendzone has scaled their outreach, connecting more than 4,000 participants over 200 gatherings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, if you are a young person with exciting ideas, please watch out for YAC Season 6, coming up.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: That is why we set up the four inaugural Youth Panels, to partner them to shape national policies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Dr Harun asked how we are harnessing our youths' creativity to shape our future and if we are tapping a wider pool of youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And they comprise a good mix of young working adults and schooling youths, each with their unique lived experiences and perspectives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I recently caught up with Damien and Salwa from the Institute of Technical College (ITE) College West and Kaplan Higher Education Institute respectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Despite their busy studies, they spent time at these meetings, and they found them very meaningful and also very valuable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They got to exchange perspectives with other members from different backgrounds and deliberate on complex issues to shape their policy recommendations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They are only 17 years old, and their level of maturity and insightfulness, and indeed, their questions, were really inspiring.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our youths have a direct role in deciding the issues that the Youth Panels would address.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, I look forward to seeing our Youth Panels' recommendations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: If you are keen to share your perspectives, please join us at our inaugural Youth Policy Forum later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our panels will present their policy ideas and debate them before finalising their recommendations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These are individuals giving back and offering peer support in neighbourhoods they grew up in or areas that are close to their heart.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: An area that is close to my heart is Jalan Kukoh, where I started my volunteering journey as a youth 20 years ago, serving children, youths, seniors and vulnerable families there.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Jalan Kukoh is now home to one of 24 SG Cares Volunteer Centres (VCs) across Singapore, making an impact in their respective communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I recently met Mrs Chan Swee Fen, a volunteer with SG Cares VC @ Kreta Ayer, which covers Jalan Kukoh.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Swee Fen has a Master's degree in counselling and trains volunteer befrienders in practical counselling skills, giving them confidence to conduct home visits and befriend vulnerable seniors in Jalan Kukoh and also the Chin Swee area.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: She is one of 20,000 volunteers who regularly serve with VCs and is a forerunner of what we call skills-based volunteerism where individuals volunteer their professional skills to meet specific community needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And more professional bodies are adopting this model of volunteering.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, MCCY is partnering Pro Bono SG to grow and develop their pool of volunteer lawyers who provide legal advice to non-profit organisations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Last December, I met Ms Cai Chengying and her Pro Bono SG team, and they told me that they will be expanding their reach beyond Tian De Temple.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: True to their word, Pro Bono SG launched their second Community Law Centre in the Northwest District earlier this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng asked about sustaining our VCs' impact and how they are strengthening volunteer management.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked about reaching senior volunteers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our VCs equip community partners with skills to attract, engage and retain volunteers of all ages – the young and the young-at-heart.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, SG Cares VCs @ Geylang and Serangoon train MOE educators to design more meaningful values-in-action (VIA) programmes and projects, encouraging students to continue volunteering even after completing their VIA requirements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our VCs also work with community partners like RSVP Singapore and Active Ageing Centres to avail more volunteering opportunities that meet the interests of seniors, such as mentoring, befriending and supporting non-profit organisations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MCCY also works with the National Council of Social Services and the Singapore University of Social Sciences to equip our VCs to better do their outreach, training, volunteer management and enable them to learn from one another's best practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Baey asked how we manage when SG Cares VCs change operators to keep up with the town's shifting needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Disruptions are limited and our volunteers have continued to serve on the ground consistently.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, those keen to volunteer with our SG Cares Volunteer Centres, please visit our SG Cares website to find your nearest VC and to learn about volunteering opportunities that match your interest and your specific skillsets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And there is no more important cause to contribute to than our precious racial and religious harmony, a point that Mr Sitoh Yi Pin, Mr Darryl David and Mr Raj Joshua Thomas made yesterday.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As what Minister Edwin Tong said, it is something we must cherish and protect.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I agree with them that we must press on with these efforts, and I am glad to say we are far from starting from scratch.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our community and religious leaders have worked hard over the years to achieve this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Leaders from key ethnic and religious groups contribute to our National Steering Committee on Racial and Religious Harmony.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This Committee has helped foster closer ties among these leaders who, in turn, bring their communities together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Committee Members even take turns to organise the annual Harmony Games.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Just last Saturday, the Catholic Archdiocese were the lead organisers and they will hand over to the Taoist Federation to organise next year's games.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: On the ground in our communities, our Racial and Religious Harmony Circles (HCs) have seen an increase in membership and activities since we refreshed them last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I have joined a few of these such activities, including last year's Harmony Sports Fiesta at our Sports Hub that reached more than 31,000 people, thanks to the support of over 1,000 HC members, and also Marymount HC's Ultimate Frisbee Tournament with over 200 youths and the young-at-heart.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Beneath the roaring energy on the field, I witnessed a shared sense of mutual trust and understanding among participants from different religious organisations and community groups at Marymount.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But our work is only just getting started and we have much more to do.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And our Harmony Circle Coordinating Council will continue to strengthen efforts to make our HCs more diverse and more digital.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, if you are passionate about preserving and strengthening our precious racial and religious harmony, please join your nearest HC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This group comprises our SG Mental Well-being Network, which Ms Hany Soh mentioned.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We set up this Network in 2022 so that individuals, community stakeholders and private partners can work together to build mental resilience in our communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The three newest well-being circles are located in Queenstown, Marymount and the Singapore Management University.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And we welcome the Woodgrove Well-being Circle as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And we have made progress beyond these community or locale well-being circles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our network's members, such as Growth Collective SG and Happiness Initiative, have introduced their own peer support programmes, running more than 900 peer support circles across workplaces, educational and healthcare institutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Studies done with selected partners found that these peer support circles helped improve mental well-being and sustain it over time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will launch a guide later this year on how to set up a Well-Being Circle.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, if you want to set up one, please connect with our network or join our Partners Networking Night on 25 March at 7.00 pm at the Lifelong Learning Institute.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Alongside our burgeoning community are corporates which have also answered the call.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I recently caught up with Razif Yusoff, who is the co-founder of Push Pull Give, a fitness social enterprise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Push Pull Give allows non-profit organisations to use their fitness studios for free and offers scholarships and employment opportunities for young adults from disadvantaged backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Push Pull Give is one of the 55 companies that have committed to the National Volunteer and Philanthropic Centre's Company of Good Programme, pledging positive social impact as the core of their business.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Corporates which actively give back to society rarely do so alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In fact, mutual support and opportunities to network with like-minded businesses are hallmarks of NVPC's Company of Good Programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: A couple of weeks ago, I visited Unilever's campus to meet 16 local small and medium enterprises (SMEs) which signed up for the Unilever-NVPC Purpose for Growth programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Unilever mentors helped these SMEs define their business strategy and how to make a positive impact in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I am sure many more companies will do the same.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I invite them to come because all companies, big and small, can play a part, work together and amplify your social impact on the ground.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I would also like to thank Mr Neil Parekh and the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) for working with us to set up the Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) Coordination Office in SBF.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I look forward to working with him and his team through quarterly industry engagements to reach SBF's 28,000 members and encourage more corporates to follow in the footsteps of Companies of Good.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi asked how we can support our Co-operatives, which are already contributing to society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I meet with our Cooperatives and Singapore National Co-operative Federation (SNCF) leaders regularly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are working closely with SNCF to groom emerging leaders and provide targeted funding to ensure our co-operatives remain relevant and also well-governed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked about the progress of Mentoring SG.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: She mentioned School of Day 1, by Matin Mohdari, which is part of Mentoring SG.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: School of Day 1 recently ran a session for youths who just received their "A" level results.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I am in contact with Matin and have promised him that we will do more together under the Mentoring SG banner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mentoring SG is embarking on a research study to measure the impact of mentoring programmes and partnerships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The findings will enable it to scale up quality programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This year, Mentoring SG will partner more corporates on industry-led mentoring initiatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It will also partner more polytechnics and ITEs, to provide more avenues for corporates to give back.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, the Singapore Semiconductor Industry Association (SSIA) partnered Mentoring SG at the recent Electronics Industry Day in ITE College Central, which I attended, and where employees from semiconductor giant Micron Electronics conducted a “flash mentoring” programme for ITE students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The students I spoke to at the event benefited greatly from the experience, they left with a newfound interest in careers within the semiconductor and precision engineering sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Corporates and individuals keen to support our national mentoring movement, please sign up at mentoring.sg.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Therefore, Mr Keith Chua’s question about how we plan to grow philanthropy and foster collaboration is timely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong shared in his Budget speech about an initiative that will help donors better appreciate the needs of our society and also direct their resources to these needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I discussed these details about The Collective with the CFS team at their 15th Anniversary Lunch three weeks ago.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: CFS will release further details later this year and I encourage companies to find out more and we are looking forward to partner as many companies as possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The Collective is one platform for our community and our corporates to give back.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We agree with Mr Baey and recognise that some of these ideas do not necessarily fall neatly along agency lines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Therefore, SGPO acts as a "first-stop" for citizens or stakeholders with such ideas and it helps to connect them to the right agencies or partners to put their ideas into action.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, please connect with us on our SGPO website with your ideas and your plans for action!

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, our community and our corporates have answered the Forward SG call for a new, refreshed social compact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: You have heard me share about the different platforms and the different spaces and the different tools we have made available for our community and our corporates, so I invite all of you to join us to take that step alongside us to shape the Singapore we all want to see, together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
