text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua will quicken our steps in his speech about sports next, so I shall hand the baton smoothly for him as he brings us to the home stretch.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Chair, sports is a great way for people from all walks of life, whether you are a senior, a youth, a person with disabilities, sport enthusiast, or weekend warrior, to bond and to stay healthy together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Singaporeans lead busy lives but we want to make it easier for everyone to make sports a way of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is made possible through the Sport Facilities Master Plan (SFMP).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These facilities are located conveniently within HDB estates and are free for use by all.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Dr Syed Harun highlighted the importance of sport in strengthening community ties and social cohesion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SIP facilities serve as organic nodes that brings the community together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: From playgrounds for children, to sheltered courts for futsal or basketball, exercise stations with QR codes which you can scan to learn correct techniques and rubberised walking tracks for seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: More than 370 facilities including indoor sports halls and free-to-play fields are also available under the Dual Use Scheme (DUS).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In fact, there are over 40 free-to-play fields where Singaporeans can freely use on weekends.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This year, we look forward to the opening of four new facilities namely: the Kallang Tennis Hub, the Kallang Football Hub, new basketball courts at the former Bedok Swimming Complex and a facility for softball and baseball at Jurong East.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In the coming years, Punggol and Clementi residents can also look forward to new sports facilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At Clementi, there will be a new town playfield which includes a running track and community sport courts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And we have been making our sporting facilities inclusive and accessible to Singaporeans of all abilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Ong Hua Han emphasised that it is not enough to just make our sports facilities inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We must help persons with disabilities feel empowered to exercise in mainstream settings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Since the launch of the Disability Sport Master Plan (DSMP) in 2016, SportSG has introduced a range of programmes so more persons with disabilities can take part in sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These include the learn-to-play programmes such as “Yes!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I Can” and “Play-Ability”, as mentioned by Minister Edwin earlier, and an annual Play Inclusive campaign.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To date, some 20,000 persons with disabilities have taken part in these programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our vision is for all persons with disabilities to be engaged, enriched, and empowered through sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To refresh the DSMP, we have convened a taskforce comprising stakeholders from SportSG, MSF, SG Enable, MOE and disability sports organisations such as the Singapore Disability Sports Council (SDSC) and Special Olympics Singapore (SOSG).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To date, the task force has engaged more than 600 stakeholders, received good inputs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In essence, the DSMP refresh will look to: one, increase accessibility to disability sport activities and facilities; two, enhance awareness of disability and inclusive sporting opportunities; and three, help fulfil the aspirations of those who aspire to pursue sports at the high performance level.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will share more in detail later this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Sport is not only a great way to keep fit, but also builds character, transforms lives and encourage social mixing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In particular, the SportCares programme seeks to harness the power of sport to provide access and opportunities for marginalised communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through SportCares initiatives and bursaries, children and youths from low-income families have increased access to quality sports programmes, such as athletics, basketball, water polo and canoeing and many others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To date, the SportCares bursaries have enabled more than 480 children and youths to learn new sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In April 2023, SportCares also awarded scholarships to its first batch of students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Hassan joined SportCares’ Saturday Night Lights (SNL) programme in 2017.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SNL is a football programme for youths aged 13 to 21, to train regularly and to compete in the HEARTS Football league throughout the year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Coming from a low-income family with his father as the sole breadwinner, Hassan is the third of five children and juggles part-time jobs to alleviate the financial strain at home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Other than studying, Hassan is also caregiver to his five-year-old younger brother.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: During his time with SportCares, Hassan served as a responsible captain of his SNL team.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As an alumnus, Hassan continues to give back by volunteering with SportCares, planning camps for students with special needs and children from low-income families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: He also participates actively in the SportCares Champions programme – a leadership programme for youths willing and able to step into the role of a leader and mentor.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With the help of the scholarship, Hassan will complete his Diploma in Sustainable Built Environment at Republic Polytechnic and he has plans to join the Police force.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We really hope more Singaporeans and corporates will step forward to donate generously to SportCares.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Chair, we know how passionate Singaporeans are when it comes to football, and how much we hope to see our national team succeed both at the regional as well as international levels.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Darryl David and Mr Faisal Manap asked for an update on Unleash the Roar and the selection process for Singapore’s National Team's Head Coach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Football Association of Singapore (FAS) is responsible for the promotion and development of the sport.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This includes developing training programmes and the hiring of coaches.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: FAS has gone through a rigorous process to find a new coach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Let us give our new national coach some time to find his footing and hopefully make his mark with the national team.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To be sure, we are playing the long game to uplift Singapore football.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (UTR!) in March 2021, and since then we have made steady progress to strengthen our football ecosystem locally.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have also set up and since sent our National Development Centre (NDC) teams and a combined SFA squad overseas for training camps and competition opportunities to expose them to quality competition they cannot find locally and to further their development in football.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Just last month, we launched the Singapore Youth League (SYL): our inaugural nationwide high performance youth football competition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The SYL provides aspiring youth players a regular and competitive platform to gain match experience and develop their football skills.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through this league, we hope to further strengthen a robust talent pipeline of next-generation national team players.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Last year, we also sent our first batch of eight young footballers on UTR!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Chloe Koh, one of our scholarship recipients, is now at the IMG Academy in the US.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Her near-term goal is to play in the NCAA Division I and, ultimately, she wants to play professionally.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As an introvert, Chloe had to step out of her comfort zone when she first arrived in the US.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: After a few months, however, she has quickly adapted.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At IMG, Chloe gets to travel to different states in the United States, play in tournaments and showcase her skills to college scouts, who are proactively seeking out young talents and potentially bringing them a step closer to their dream of turning professional.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We wish Chloe and all our UTR scholars currently overseas all the best.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Chair, our Team Singapore athletes continue to inspire Singaporeans as they shine on the world stage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And this is only possible with a strong support system backing them in taking their sporting goals to the next level.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our high-performance sport (HPS) system is dynamic and athlete-centric.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Each athlete is supported in a holistic and personalised manner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Singapore Sport and Exercise Medicine Centre (SSMC@SSI) provides personalised sport medicine care for our athletes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Such support includes comprehensive medical screening, focusing on both physical as well as mental health; support for athlete recovery through physiotherapy and exercise rehabilitation; and integration of medical care with sports sciences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Athletes are covered by a medical insurance policy that allows athletes to claim for in-patient treatment or surgery for accidental sports-related injuries not covered by SSI or SSMC@SSI.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To Ms Sylvia Lim's suggestion regarding former national athletes, our consistent approach is to support our athletes' transition into retirement from the competitive sporting careers by helping them find good employment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Active and retired athletes can also tap on various programmes, including spexEducation and spexBusiness, as elaborated by the Minister in his speech earlier.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But we will explore how we can support them better.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On the funding of NSAs, there is no change to the policy and requirements that NSAs must meet to qualify for our funding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Besides the mandatory annual submission of audited statement of accounts to SportSG, NSAs are also required to allow SportSG to audit their accounting records.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: If an NSA is found non-compliant with the terms of its funding agreement, SportSG will take appropriate action, such as suspending, terminating or even recovering the grant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For more serious cases, such as misappropriation of funds, SportSG would refer these to the police.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have also previously explained, how we allocate our funding across the NSAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SportSG's annual grants to NSAs help to support their organisation functions, outreach programmes, training facilities and HPS plans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Annually, the level of funding is assessed holistically, considering a few factors, such as its alignment with SportSG's Vision 2030, whether it has achieved agreed KPIs, its capabilities in governance and execution and the existence of a sound plan for development of the sport overall.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For emerging sports that do not receive support from an NSA, funded directly by SportSG, Mr Darryl David and Mr Mohd Fahmi asked about how we can support aspiring athletes in these fields.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Athletes can apply as individuals or as a team.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Applications for the March window will be from 1 to 31 March, so please start applying.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Another key component of our athlete support system are our coaches.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Jean See will be pleased to know that we are looking to upskill and professionalise exercise, sports and outdoor adventure coaches and instructors, which in turn, could increase their wages that is commensurate with their skillset.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For exercise professionals, SportSG will be instituting an accreditation framework under the National Registry for Exercise Professionals (NREP) in a later phase and we welcome inputs from NICA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Jean See would also understand that the exercise, sports and outdoor adventure sectors are diverse with niche offerings and therefore it is difficult to introduce a cost norm.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, we will continue to engage coaches to better understand their challenges and explore ways to further support them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For example, in the outdoor adventure sector, the Outdoor Adventure Education (OAE) Council is working on a capability development roadmap that will look into the salary and remuneration challenges for full-time and freelance OAE professionals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are open to see how SkillsFuture can further support their professional development and the OAE Council will also be looking at having more sites and facilities with affordable access.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (In Mandarin):   Sports help us maintain physical and mental health and is also one of the ways to build character, transform lives and encourage social mixing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Government supports children and youths from different backgrounds to participate in sports through ActiveSG’s Academies and Clubs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In particular, the SportSG’s SportCares programme is committed to providing opportunities for marginalised groups to participate in sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We hope that more Singaporeans and corporates can generously donate and actively contribute to SportCares. : Chair, through sports, we can grow closer as a community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through sports, we can improve our health and instil a sense of confidence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through sports, we can inspire a nation to go beyond our limits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So, I hope to rally all Singaporeans to take action today and let us all live better through sports.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have a clarification for Minister of State Low.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The move to harness the power of arts to improve well-being is laudable.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can the Minister of State share more on this initiative and the benefits that participation in the arts and cultural activities can bring to our seniors?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Chairman, I want to thank the Member Ms Joan Pereira.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: She spoke very passionately during her cut delivery last evening about this.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Actually, she has been consistently giving feedback to MCCY to see how we can synergise our workstream with our MOH counterparts.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Indeed, the arts can be harnessed to support greater well-being, empowering individuals to lead healthier and more fulfilling lives.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, we really encourage all Singaporeans: please get involved in the arts and cultural activities.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Then, we will open up for other segments later – Singaporeans and to expand arts access and the range of work of our arts and cultural practitioners.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One clarification, which I believe could be for Minister of State Alvin.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As many societies are being divided by issues and conflicts with ethnic and religious undertones, what are we doing specifically to pull our society together?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And how are we in, our own small part, contributing to global efforts to build more cohesive societies?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As Minister Edwin mentioned, MCCY really brings up the end of the Committee of Supply debate.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Our heart must be strong, it must be united.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It cannot be split, it cannot be divided.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But at times it is also moved, moved by issues that confront us, issues that affront us.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Over the last couple of months, I have hosted a few of these very spiky dialogues.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There was one I hosted with our Harmony Circle leaders on the Gaza crisis.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It was not easy to do, but it allowed for our leaders a safe space to discuss, to air and to also explain their perspectives.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Today, this afternoon, I am going to host two young advocates as well.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It is going to be a place for space, for platforms.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I also mentioned earlier on that we are equipping our Harmony Circle leaders with the tools in which to touch on and engage in these very spiky issues.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: You would have known that many of the Harmony Circles came together to raise funds for the Gaza crisis, the humanitarian crisis there, and we will continue to do so.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But I also want to take us a step back and think about, because the Member mentioned cohesive societies.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We have had two iterations of the International Conference on Cohesive Societies.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These two editions, we brought together of about a thousand leaders and youth from about 30 countries.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They came, they discussed what it meant to be and how do you build Cohesive Societies.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We brought them to our heartlands, we brought them to our Harmony Circles.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: One feedback that came out of it was, how do you preserve and protect the social and racial and religious cohesion that you have in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, it dawned upon me and many of our Members that it is something that, as what Minister Edwin said, we have to cherish and we have to protect.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I still remember hosting some youths from Myanmar and they were fresh off the Rohingya crisis.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We brought them to Chinatown and we showed them the Fairfield Methodist Church, Buddha Tooth Relic Temple, Chulia Mosque as well as Sri Mariamman Temple.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It is something that we take for granted.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They said this could never happen in their country.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, when we engage in these dialogues, I think it is very important that we also, as we preserve, we want to make sure that in these dialogues, that we remember what we have and we continue to cherish all of that together.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, we will have more of these dialogues, we will create the spaces, the platforms, as well as the tools to preserve this precious racial and religious harmony.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have a clarification for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Chua on supporting retired athletes.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Earlier on, he ended off that response with this open-ended statement to say that the Ministry would explore how we could support former athletes better.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I would like him to clarify whether this includes possibly looking at how we can support the healthcare needs of our retired athletes, especially for conditions which were associated with their sporting careers, because I think it is a very meaningful gesture that society can make.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The short answer is yes, because we are looking at how we can support our retired athletes more holistically.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: I just have one clarification and that is on Gillman Barracks.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Will MCCY be working with the Ministry of National Development (MND) to ensure that the artistic character of the space is preserved and what will be the plans for existing tenants of the space?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Chairman, I want to thank Ms Usha Chandradas on the question of Gillman Barracks.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure Ms Usha Chandradas and also arts tenants at Gillman Barracks and, in fact, our arts and culture sector that NAC will certainly work with the relevant agency – MND, HDB, SLA and also URA – to support the art tenants where possible and if some of them are planning and thinking of relocation, we will certainly work together with the relevant agencies to facilitate their relocation.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, supporting them and pointing them to available spaces that they can possibly consider.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure the Member that we are committed to supporting the development of a vibrant and sustainable arts sector in Singapore and that involves supporting our artists, programme activation and of course, providing spaces.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: If I can take one minute to share with Ms Usha Chandradas and, in fact, the sector, they would have observed that, in fact, in the last few years we can see that the visual arts sector has really continued to grow and flourish over the years.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It was mentioned a bit earlier but it bears repeating again.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Tanjong Pagar District Park is a very exciting and evolving space with the Singapore Art Museum and also a number of art galleries and art businesses currently sited there.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Both Minister Edwin Tong and myself talked about Singapore Art Week 2023 and Singapore Art Week 2024.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: NAC has also supported the growing creative developments at the Tanjong Pagar District Park through programmes, such as the sonic sessions during the Singapore Art Week 2024 this year featuring the performances by local musicians and artists.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Singapore also plays host to leading showcases and art fair, such as the recently concluded ArtSG which saw a line-up of 114 galleries from 33 countries and territories, attracting a record attendance of more than 45,000 visitors during the 2024 edition, the one that just recently concluded.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure the Member that the NAC's arts infrastructure and spaces have grown over the years.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure the Member that we will be working very closely with our MND counterparts and their agency to give the necessary support to the art tenants.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I also want to assure the Member that we will work with the partners in the arts and culture sector to develop a vibrant and sustainable arts sector.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: First is in relation to providing more support to inspire our young to embrace and pursue their passion in sports.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I am heartened to hear from the Minister's speech that there will be more sporting opportunities, for example, through inter-school sports tournaments.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: However, I do hope that the Ministry can continue its efforts to urge other stakeholders, for example, like the Singapore Sports School, to do more in the community, with the community, for the community.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Some examples can be done through events that are jointly organised with the grassroots.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For example, like a badminton clinic in which our Woodgrove CSC has organised with partners, such as Singapore Badminton Association and SportsSG, where the Team Singapore athletes, our shuttlers came forward.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Apart from imparting their skills, they also take the opportunity to share more about their own personal experience, how they have come through all of the challenges to becoming a professional sportsman.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The second clarification is on the Sports Facilities Master Plan.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Apart from constructing and upgrading our current facilities that are operated by the ActiveSG, I wonder if we are also looking into working closely with MOE and its schools to offer more of their sporting facilities to the community.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Take, for example, in Woodgrove where Innova Primary, has come forward to share with our Woodgrove CSC on a weekly basis its sports hall every Friday evening to organise badminton sessions for the community.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: If the Member had listened to my speech, there are a lot of plans coming up as part of the Sports Facilities Master Plan.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Other than the Member, Mr Ong Hua Han has also mentioned that it is not just the hardware.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It is also about the heart ware, what keeps the heart ware going.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It is as much as it is about the hardware as it is about the software or the programmes that are running in the institutions.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We take the Member's point about having more programmes to collaborate with the schools, more programmes to collaborate with the community.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In fact, if the Member had listened in to some of what I said for football earlier, the Member would know that a lot of it is vested and intertwined within our school system.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Across all the different checkboxes, schools, different genders and different sporting types, we are trying to do more of that, to popularise and propagate more sports, and working in collaboration with the community.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The first is relating to the Major Sports Events Fund.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: My appeal is that for the Major Sports Events Fund, it will also provide learning opportunities for freelancers and ancillary services, for example, those doing content production in audio-visual (AV) and whether there can be learning opportunities for them to also shadow the international teams.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Of course, the learning opportunities could also extend to Singaporeans who can front opening acts as well as festivals that accompany these major events.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The second clarification is for Minister of State Low Yen Ling.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: For the SG Arts Plan, this is something very exciting.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: I just wanted to put across a point that while professional development is good, the other part is how we enable sustainable businesses.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: One of the biggest concerns is relating to payments or non-payments, contracts issues, as well as also safe work practices.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: I just wanted to put forth a proposal to the Ministry that in conceptualising the SG Arts Plan, whether this can be one of the agenda items in terms of looking at the sustainable practices and working with stakeholders like NICA and the Visual, Audio, Creative Content Professionals Association, Singapore (VICPA) to put this as one of the agenda in developing the arts ecosystem in Singapore.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The third clarification to Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: We certainly welcome the Athletes Inspire Fund for emerging Sports.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The ask is that for the coaches who are supporting these athletes in emerging sports, that there could also be more support in terms of their professional development.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Indeed, like many other grants and funds that we have, we will use them strategically.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is focused on bringing major sports events into Singapore, invigorate the system here.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And as I mentioned earlier also, using the platform of these major international sporting events and the quality of those events to support the development of our local athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I want to cite two examples to the Member to illustrate what I mean.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is not just about learning how to organise such an event and learning the ropes and understanding how it is done and getting the know-how, organisational know-how, but also being a partner with many of the parties.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Many Singapore companies, SMEs were involved in part of the running of the programme on a contract basis.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the same way, we are now hosting the World Table Tennis Smash in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These two examples, I hope, assure Ms See that whenever we use the Fund, there will always be a strategic goal behind what else we can do to impact Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Chairman, I want to thank the Member, Ms See, for the suggestion on the sustainable practices.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure her that in MCCY and also NAC, we are aligned with NICA.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In fact, I recall coming into MCCY, it was during the COVID-19 years, so we had many Zoom sessions with NICA and the various agencies.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We pulled this whole-of-Government, multi-agency committee together to support our SEPs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Like what Minister Edwin Tong has mentioned, more than a third of our arts and cultural practitioners are freelancers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We are certainly aligned with the Member in supporting them, in terms of strengthening their resilience, in terms of enhancing and ensuring better career stability.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: That is why we made the announcement today.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Arts Resource Hub is a very important place for our SEPs, not only as a co-working space for collaboration, but also a place for them to sort of attend some of these important courses, whether it is digital literacy, financial literacy and so on.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: CoachSG will work with relevant agencies and bodies like NICA to be sure that our coaches are well-supported.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: It would be very helpful to know a bit more about this and what it might look like as we move this into fruition.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: For example, is the focus on strong collaborative philanthropy to help our community?

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Will it galvanise all our community together in this effort, recognising that the key players in this are the Community Foundation of Singapore, the Ministry of Social and Family Development, Community Chest and supported by MCCY?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister of State Alvin Tan, we are approaching our guillotine time.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I hope your response will be a short one.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, you have these resources and then, you have these needs.

speaker: The Chairman
text: With that last clarification and response, can I invite Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, if you like, to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank all Members of Parliament for their speeches and the MCCY team for their effort and hard work.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: With that, Sir, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
